50: New Moon: This phase occurs when the Moon is directly between the Earth and the Sun, making the side of the Moon facing Earth completely dark and therefore not visible from our planet. It marks the beginning of a new lunar cycle.

Waxing Crescent: During this phase, a small, sliver-shaped portion of the Moon's right side (as observed from the Northern Hemisphere) becomes illuminated and visible from Earth. "Waxing" means it is growing in illumination, and "crescent" refers to its curved shape. This phase continues until about 7 days after the New Moon.

First Quarter: Also known as the Half Moon, this phase is when exactly half of the Moon's face is illuminated, specifically the right half (from the Northern Hemisphere perspective). It occurs approximately 7 to 8 days after the New Moon, and the Moon appears as a perfect D-shape. At this point, the Moon has completed one quarter of its orbit around the Earth.

Waxing Gibbous: In this phase, more than half but not all of the Moon's face is illuminated. The illuminated portion continues to grow larger each day, moving towards the Full Moon. The term "gibbous" refers to the shape, which is bulging or convex. This phase occurs between the First Quarter and Full Moon.

Full Moon: This is the most striking phase, occurring when the entire side of the Moon facing Earth is fully illuminated by the Sun, appearing as a complete circle in the sky. This happens approximately 14 to 15 days after the New Moon, roughly halfway through the lunar cycle. The Earth is between the Sun and the Moon during this phase.

Waning Gibbous: After the Full Moon, the illuminated portion of the Moon begins to decrease. During the Waning Gibbous phase, more than half of the Moon is still illuminated, but the lit area is shrinking from the right side towards the left (from the Northern Hemisphere perspective). "Waning" means decreasing. This phase occurs between the Full Moon and the Last Quarter.

Last Quarter: Also known as the Third Quarter or Half Moon, this phase is when exactly half of the Moon's face is illuminated, specifically the left half (from the Northern Hemisphere perspective). It occurs approximately 22 days after the New Moon, and the Moon appears as a perfect C-shape. At this point, the Moon has completed three quarters of its orbit around the Earth.

Waning Crescent: This is the final illuminated phase before the New Moon. Only a small, sliver-shaped portion of the Moon's left side (as observed from the Northern Hemisphere) remains illuminated and visible from Earth. The illuminated area continues to shrink each day until it disappears entirely, leading back to the New Moon, completing the lunar cycle. This phase occurs between the Last Quarter and the New Moon.
